#### 8.1 Analysis 1: Comparative Clinical Performance and Safety of Autobolus vs. Temporary Basal Dosing Strategies

Objective: Demonstrate that the transition from a temp basal dosing strategy with presets to an autobolus dosing strategy and presets is non-inferior to temp basal delivery with respect to percent TIR (70–180 mg/dL), using a pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 5%.

Sample: N = `{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "N", "count")` users with valid TB→AB transition segments after applying CGM coverage (≥70% of 14-day period) and pump settings guardrail exclusion filters. `{python} cell("derived", "guardrail_excluded_users", "value", "count")` users were excluded for having settings outside guardrails.

Non-Inferiority Assessment

The mean paired difference in TIR (70–180 mg/dL) was `{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff Mean ± SD", "signed:2", part="mean_sd.mean", null=0)` percentage points (SD = `{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff Mean ± SD", "decimal:2", part="mean_sd.sd")`), with a 95% confidence interval of [`{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff 95% CI", "decimal:2", part="interval.low", null=-5)`, `{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff 95% CI", "decimal:2", part="interval.high")`]. The lower bound of the 95% CI (`{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff 95% CI", "signed:2", part="interval.low", null=-5)`) exceeds the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of −5 percentage points. Therefore, autobolus delivery with presets is non-inferior to temp basal delivery with presets with respect to time in range.

Additionally, the paired t-test (p = `{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "p (paired t-test)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`) and Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p = `{python} cell("nonparametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "p (Wilcoxon signed-rank)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`) both indicate a statistically significant improvement in TIR during the autobolus period.

Summary of Findings

Across the `{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "N", "count")` paired user segments, the transition from temp basal to autobolus delivery was associated with a statistically significant increase in time in range (70–180 mg/dL) of `{python} cell("parametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff Mean ± SD", "signed:2", part="mean_sd.mean", null=0)` percentage points (median `{python} cell("nonparametric", "Time 70–180 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff Median [IQR]", "signed:2", part="median_iqr.median", null=0)`). Time above range (>180 mg/dL) decreased by `{python} cell("derived", "time_above_180_decrease", "value", "decimal:2", null=0)` percentage points and time above 250 mg/dL decreased by `{python} cell("derived", "time_above_250_decrease", "value", "decimal:2", null=0)` percentage points (both p < 0.001). Mean glucose decreased by `{python} cell("derived", "mean_glucose_decrease", "value", "decimal:2", null=0)` mg/dL (p = `{python} cell("parametric", "Mean glucose (mg/dL)", "p (paired t-test)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`).

Time below 54 mg/dL (p = `{python} cell("parametric", "Time <54 mg/dL (%)", "p (paired t-test)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`), hypoglycemic event rate (p = `{python} cell("parametric", "Hypoglycemic events (n/14 d)", "p (paired t-test)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`), and coefficient of variation (p = `{python} cell("parametric", "Coefficient of variation (%)", "p (paired t-test)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`) showed no statistically significant difference across delivery strategies. Time below 70 mg/dL showed a small increase of `{python} cell("parametric", "Time <70 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff Mean ± SD", "signed:2", part="mean_sd.mean", null=0)` percentage points that did not reach significance on the paired t-test (p = `{python} cell("parametric", "Time <70 mg/dL (%)", "p (paired t-test)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`); the non-parametric Wilcoxon test was significant (p(WSRT) = `{python} cell("nonparametric", "Time <70 mg/dL (%)", "p (Wilcoxon signed-rank)", "p_scientific", part="p_equals.value")`, median `{python} cell("nonparametric", "Time <70 mg/dL (%)", "Paired Diff Median [IQR]", "signed:2", part="median_iqr.median", null=0)`). However, this small increase was not accompanied by statistically significant differences in more consequential hypoglycemia metrics, including Time below 54 mg/dL or hypoglycemic event rate. Taken together, these results indicate that improvements in time in range and reductions in hyperglycemia observed with autobolus were achieved without evidence of a meaningful increase in hypoglycemia risk relative to temporary basal delivery.

The Shapiro-Wilk test indicated significant departures from normality for paired differences across all glycemic endpoints (all Shapiro p < 0.001). However, non-parametric results were consistent with parametric results for all endpoints.
